report.summary: Reviewed the read-only plan against the supplied packet. The key question is whether a new `locked_price_match` restoration can safely reuse the existing `locked_price_mismatch` guard path in `lib/assessment-source-publication.ts` (lines 48-53). It cannot safely reuse that path in its current form. The guard sets `sourcePublicationGuard = "locked_price_mismatch"` at line 334 in `lib/delivery-assessment.ts` during the `changes_suggested`-only branch (line 331), which never handles a raw/current `supported` model item with unknown or unverified business price facts. If a `locked_price_match` reason is added and the guard is set there, then simply checking that every price check is `unchanged` (e.g. `independent.checks.some(c => c.kind === "unknown")` as at line 53) is insufficient: the citation witness required by the plan would not be tied into the restoration gate. As a result, a positive restoration could publish a canonical supported status backed only by business-check facts, without the model citations covering each complete original owner span, and without confirming that the other later guards (presence, exact copy, native, label, tag, list, target, verbatim) would also stay exactly as the canonical decision requires. Secondary weaknesses are in the plan's fail-closed handling: it adds a new direct `reason` value and a separate positive replay. Those must be kept consistent with the export/audit surface, and the positive restore must be limited to `encoding === "catalog_slots"` because the existing guard is only captured on that path. Also, the fixture (lines 218-726) retains no provider HTTP body or prompt, so the positive path can be exercised only with the synthesized envelope that the fixture labels (lines 8-10, 727).

findings.title: Price-match restoration can't be driven by a guard flag that is only set inside the changes_suggested branch
findings.evidence: Line 331 runs the business-evidence downgrade block only when `status === "changes_suggested"`. Line 334 inside it does `sourcePublicationGuard = "locked_price_mismatch"; status = "insufficient_evidence"`. `sourcePublicationCheck` is called at lines 512-515 with `rawStatus: modelJudgment.status`, `guardedStatus: status`, and `guardReason: sourcePublicationGuard`. A raw/current `supported` item with an all-unknown or unsupported price check carries no guard flag at lines 512-515. Also, in the positive path the code branches at line 373 (`literal?.kind === "covered"`) and line 388 (witness), and both shadow the local `business` and never set `sourcePublicationGuard`. So the plan's instruction to "try positive restoration INSIDE actual supported business unknown branch" has no matching branch in the current code. The positive restore therefore has to be added either as a new flag set at a new site, with how it interacts with the line 334 value fixed, or at line 512, where `modelJudgment.status === "supported"` and the business check is `unchanged`.
findings.reproduction: Reasoning trace (not executed): the fixture `coverage-1` (lines 471-527) has `modelJudgment.status: "supported"` and `sourceFinding.status: "supported"`, while its business checks (`business-1` and `business-2`, lines 114-147, `menu.html`, `item_price` AUD1800) are legitimately `unchanged`. Under the plan, the guard is set only in the `changes_suggested` branch, which `supported` items never reach. At line 512 `guardReason` is therefore `undefined` and line 38 of `lib/assessment-source-publication.ts` returns `undefined`. No restore happens, and the saved result stays `insufficient_evidence` even though direct-source facts are supported. If instead the implementer sets the flag at line 388/373 and reuses the mismatch block, line 49 requires `fact.basis === "locked_business_values"` (true), but line 53 accepts any independent `mismatch` and any citation that exists. That does not require the model citations to exactly cover every complete owner span returned by `assessSourceBusinessCitationWitness`, which the plan requires for EVERY check. The canonical decision is therefore not established.
findings.suggestion: Add a distinct new guard branch, e.g. `locked_price_match`, with these conditions: (1) it is set only where `modelJudgment.status === "supported"` (not gated on `status === "changes_suggested"`); (2) the branch requires `legacy.kind === "unknown"` with all checks `dynamic_or_unsupported_source`; (3) `independent.kind === "unchanged"` with all checks `unchanged` and cited; (4) `priceFacts(criterion.id)` returns `covered`, where every witness check is `covered` and every `expected.file`, `start`, `end`, and `excerpt` equals the independent check citation; (5) `fact.status === "changes_suggested"` is replaced by `fact.status === "supported"` and `fact.basis === "locked_business_values"` with full 2..6 citations on the exact match; (6) the locked step is `item_price`; and (7) the positive branch holds only when `fact`'s citation set is the same as the model-cited owner set. Otherwise it returns `undefined`. Do not reuse the mismatch block as-is.

findings.title: Positive guard precondition (guardedStatus insufficient_evidence plus guardReason) is incompatible with the positive scenario
findings.evidence: Line 38 requires `candidate.rawStatus !== "changes_suggested" || candidate.guardedStatus !== "insufficient_evidence" || !candidate.guardReason` to return `undefined`. A canonical positive decision means the raw is `supported` and must publish as `supported`, not `insufficient_evidence`. The existing `SourcePublicationDecision` type (line 21) hard-codes `status: "changes_suggested"`, and the caller at line 517 unconditionally assigns `status = sourcePublication.status`. Reusing this funnel would force the canonical supported status through a `changes_suggested` decision object. That contradicts the plan requirement that the final status and explanation stay exactly the same canonical decision, while `modelJudgment` (lines 292-295) keeps the original explanation untrimmed.
findings.reproduction: Reasoning trace (not executed): a guarded positive item with `guardedStatus: "insufficient_evidence"` and `guardReason: "locked_price_match"` passes lines 38-39 if the reason enum is widened (line 10). Line 63 then returns `status: "changes_suggested"` with `explanation: fact.explanation`. Line 517 overwrites the local `status` to `changes_suggested`, and line 522 records `publicationBasis.reason`. The positive restore would publish a changes_suggested decision, not the canonical supported decision that the plan requires to be preserved exactly.
findings.suggestion: Widen `SourcePublicationDecision` to carry `status: ProofAssessmentItem["status"]` derived from the branch, and let the positive branch accept `rawStatus === "supported"`. The positive branch must return `status: "supported"` with the canonical independent-fact explanation, and set `checkedCitations` to the witness-covered owner citations. Only emit the publication marker when the finalized `{status, explanation, citations}` is byte-equal to the canonical supported decision. If the canonical decision is insufficient_evidence, return `undefined`.

findings.title: Positive restore placement must re-run the later guards before the marker is emitted
findings.evidence: The guard is evaluated at lines 512-520, after the label source fact at lines 498-509 and after all supported-only checks (lines 368-466). A positive restoration placed there skips lines 368-466 for the restored item, because they run earlier on the downgraded `insufficient_evidence` status. Also, `evidenceNeed` is cleared at line 519 even for a positive path. The plan requires every later guard to be re-evaluated and the explanation to stay exactly the canonical decision. Neither is structurally guaranteed by the current placement.
findings.reproduction: Reasoning trace (not executed): `presenceCheck`, `exactCopyCheck`, `nativeCitationCheck`, `labelCitationCheck`, `universalTagCheck`, and `universalListCheck` only run inside `if (status === "supported")` blocks. A price item downgraded to `insufficient_evidence` skips them, is later restored by the new guard, and is returned as `supported` without those checks ever running. That violates the plan's requirement that a positive marker appear only if every later guard's outcome equals the canonical decision.
findings.suggestion: Put the positive restoration at the point where the canonical decision is computed, i.e., run a dedicated positive pipeline that re-evaluates lines 400-509 on the restored supported status. Emit `publicationBasis` only if the resulting status, explanation, and sourceFinding citation set equal the canonical ones computed for the same inputs. Alternatively, document and enforce that the positive restore may only be applied to criteria for which the downstream checks are provably `not_applicable`, and otherwise fail closed.

findings.title: source_text scope and no-fail rule excludes coverage-1 under assessmentEvidenceScope canonicalization
findings.evidence: Line 40 requires `assessmentEvidenceScope(criterion).category === "source_text"` and no `ruleEvidence` finding of `fail`. The fixture `coverage-1` (lines 40-43) has source "菜单的牛肉面和Beef noodles标价必须为AUD18。" and title "原始需求 1". It is a coverage-derived criterion. If the evidence scope classifies it as anything other than `source_text` (for example, an unclassified coverage requirement), the positive restoration never runs. The plan restricts the change to "sourceFinding supported", but `sourceFinding` can be `supported` for `locked_business_values` even when `assessmentEvidenceScope` is not `source_text` (lines 37-48 of `assessment-source-findings.ts`).
findings.reproduction: Reasoning trace (not executed): the fixture's `coverage-1.modelJudgment` is supported with a supported `sourceFinding`, but the plan's guard requires `source_text` scope. The scope helper in `assessment-evidence-scope.ts` is not in the packet, so this can't be confirmed or excluded. This is a reliance hazard: if `coverage-1` is classified `unclassified_requirement`, the new branch is dead code for the target fixture and the "positive" cycle would produce no observable change.
findings.suggestion: Confirm offline from the supplied `criterion` and `ruleEvidence` that `assessmentEvidenceScope(criterion).category === "source_text"` and that the evidence finding is `needs_human` (not `fail`) for `coverage-1` before relying on this branch. If the scope helper classifies `coverage-*` criteria as observation or unclassified, add an explicit, narrowly typed `locked_business_values` price variant to the scope check and do not widen it to other categories.

findings.title: Fixture risk and withheldRisks retention remain tied to item_status_adjusted replay
findings.evidence: The fixture keeps `withheldRisks.reason: "item_status_adjusted"` (line 695) for `coverage-1`. A successful positive restore changes the published status back to `supported`. The materiality of this retained risk (lines 707-718) and the adjusted criteria list (lines 693-702) would then be inconsistent with the restored status. The plan claims the negative postguard logic is unchanged. The fixture retains the exact prior shape, so the replay expectation should change only for `publicationPolicy.reconciledCriterionIds` and item status, not for the withheld-risk semantics.
findings.reproduction: Reasoning trace (not executed): currently the publication policy records `reconciledCriterionIds: []` (lines 682-685), and `withheldRisks.adjustedCriteria` records `coverage-1` supported→insufficient (lines 696-702). If the positive marker appears, `reconciledCriterionIds` includes `coverage-1`. The `withheldRisks` object is derived in `publishSourceAssessmentNotes` (not in the packet) from `originalStatuses`. The restored final status is `supported`, so whether the withheld risk is still withheld depends on that helper's inputs. Any change there would be a behavioral change outside the stated scope, and it is unverifiable from the packet.
findings.suggestion: Keep `publishSourceAssessmentNotes` and the `originalStatuses` input unchanged. Add the export replay assertion only for the new positive fields (`publicationBasis.reason: "locked_price_match"`, status supported, reconciled criterion id). Do not alter or re-derive `withheldRisks` semantics in this cycle; state that withheld-risk handling for restored positives is a follow-up and must not silently change.

findings.title: Reason enum and export replay surface must be extended atomically with the new branch
findings.evidence: Line 10 defines `SourcePublicationGuardReason` with only `"locked_price_mismatch"|"confirmed_form_label_absence"`. `SourcePublicationDecision.publicationBasis.reason` is this type. Lines 522 and 564 surface it as `publicationBasis` and `publicationPolicy.reconciledCriterionIds`. Adding `"locked_price_match"` without the corresponding export replay assertion would leave the new reason unverified in saved exports.
findings.reproduction: Reasoning trace (not executed): a report saved with `publicationBasis.reason: "locked_price_match"` would be serialized. Any consumer that validates `reason` against the old union or replays only the two negative families would either reject the report or silently omit the new reason from replay. That would contradict the plan's "positive status-specific replay".
findings.suggestion: Extend the union type, the offline export consistency replay, and the saved-export validator in the same change. The replay must recompute the positive branch from the retained `sourceFinding` and model citations and assert `publicationBasis.reason === "locked_price_match"` only when the canonical result is supported.

findings.title: Legacy unknown-reason check is stricter than the fixture requires and is not anchored to the exact expected reason
findings.evidence: Line 52 requires `legacy.checks.some(c => c.kind === "unknown")` and every unknown reason to be exactly `dynamic_or_unsupported_source`. The fixture's `menu.html` contains a `<template>` with duplicate "牛肉面 AUD18" text (line 158). The legacy checker uses `hasUncertainDeclaredPriceSourceAtFile`, so this would be `dynamic_or_unsupported_source` only if that helper treats template content as uncertain. The plan also adds a template guard, which must not double-classify. More importantly, the legacy check only verifies that every unknown is dynamic; it does not require the check's `file` or expected label to exactly match the independent check's file and expected label. The independent and legacy checks are separate parses, so they could in principle disagree about which checks are unknown while still passing line 52.
findings.reproduction: Reasoning trace (not executed): for two locked checks on `menu.html`, a legacy unknown due to a whole-file uncertainty plus a legacy `unchanged` for the same item can occur only if the two parsers differ. The positive branch would then rest on a logically mixed premise (legacy says unknown, independent says unchanged), and the plan's "exact original raw supported plus actual supported-business_unknown" is only partly enforced.
